testbench.name: comparator-offset-mc
testbench.description: Monte-Carlo input-referred offset of the comparator front end over PVT, plus the part of that offset that moves across a +/-50 mV input-common-mode band, plus a null control showing this PDK models no resistor local mismatch.
testbench.claim: REFERENCE, NOT VERDICT. sim/dut.json binds design/comparator.spice (id comparator-dr0001, provenance schematic -- topology per spec/decision-records/DR-0001-comparator-topology.md). This bench measures README.md#target-specification's Offset-sigma row (<= 15 mV 3-sigma input-referred, <= 8 mV stretch) via gf180mcu's sw_stat_mismatch local-mismatch models, but that row is still DRAFT -- no decision record ratifies it -- so a measured pass or miss here is same-PDK/same-design context for the eventual ratification, not a pass/fail claim against a ratified spec.

sig_vos_mv.description: MISMATCH-ON GUARD, not a spec bound. design.ngspice defaults sw_stat_mismatch = 0, so a deck that failed to turn local mismatch on would report ~0 here while every other number in the record still looked plausible. 0.05 mV is far below anything a real 180 nm input pair can achieve, so this floor cannot be read as a design assertion -- it only catches a collapsed (mismatch-free) population. The SPEC bound (<= 15 mV 3-sigma, README.md) is deliberately NOT encoded as a check while sim/dut.json binds a placeholder: a placeholder passing or failing a spec row would be meaningless either way.

av_sigma_pct.description: LOAD-BEARING SELF-CHECK, not a design number. Each draw's gain is taken as (DC point at +2 mV minus DC point at 0 mV) within ONE `dc` sweep, which is only valid if the Monte-Carlo draw is constant across that sweep. If the draw were re-rolled per sweep point, (dv1 - dv0) would be dominated by the difference of two independent offsets rather than by the 2 mV probe, and the extracted gain would scatter by tens of percent. A few percent here is the proof that the draw was preserved, and therefore that every V_os in this record is a real offset rather than a difference of two populations.

sig_rpair_uv.description: NULL CONTROL: 1-sigma resistance mismatch of two identical ppolyf_u_1k loads, read as 1 uA times their difference. EXPECTED TO BE ZERO. gf180mcu wires `*(1+mis_r*sw_stat_mismatch)` into every resistor subckt but hard-sets mis_r = 0 and leaves the area-scaled agauss expression commented out, so this PDK models no resistor local mismatch at all. That means the offset sigma above contains NO load-mismatch contribution and that term must be budgeted by hand. As a live check rather than a comment it is a regression guard: a PDK revision that switches mis_r on fails here instead of silently changing every offset record in this repo.

mean_vos_sem.description: SYMMETRY CHECK, expressed in standard errors of the mean so it is independent of whatever sigma the bound DUT happens to have. The population mean offset must be ~0 because the circuit is nominally symmetric; +/-5 standard errors is a ~6e-7 two-sided false-alarm rate at this N. A mean outside it means a systematic asymmetry is riding on top of the mismatch -- a netlist error, or a genuinely asymmetric topology.

vbias_anchor_mv.description: CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR. The bias pin's own voltage is a V_th proxy and is strongly corner- and temperature-dependent, unlike the mismatch sigma above, which is corner-invariant almost by construction (A_Vt lives in the PDK's fets_mm subcircuits, not in any corner section). Without an anchor this manifest would have nothing that could fail under `--sabotage-corners`, and its headline numbers would stay 'valid' with the corner runner stuck on typical. It is deliberately measured on `ibn`, a CONTRACT node (the DUT's ibias pin), not on an internal node, so it survives a DUT swap. RECALIBRATED for DR-0001 (issue #12): the floors below were originally calibrated against the placeholder DUT's first committed record (process 27.35 %, temperature 14.76 % observed) and did not transfer -- `comparator_dut_analog`'s bias-mirror node (`XMB`/`XMT`, both L = 4 um) is far less temperature-sensitive at this sizing than the placeholder's was, though still comfortably corner-sensitive on the process axis. Floors are now calibrated from the full 45-point mos grid measured in this experiment's first schematic-provenance record (`comparator-dr0001`, named in this experiment's README.md), with ~45 % margin below the observed weakest slice, following the sibling repo's calibrate-from-a-cited-clean-tree-record convention. Observed weakest slices there: process 23.55 %, temperature 1.282 %. The supply axis is deliberately unfloored: a diode-connected mirror's gate voltage is set by the forced bias current and is essentially supply-independent by design, so a floor there would fail for a correct circuit.
